title: What an owner's browser gets in the admin
grade_reasons: D, at the top of the band; I recomputed the figures from the build's own stats and they hold. Every one of the 432 signed-in screens loads about 1.15 MB of script where about 0.65 MB will do, 27 screens load an editor or a catalogue they never draw (up to 4.27 MB), every screen makes 23 to 46 requests nobody asked for, and a product editor's document is two thirds unread words; budgets watch 9 of 449 routes, about 4% above figures that already hold the waste, and none of the worst four. It is not an E, because nobody is hurt yet and most of the fix is import lines; it is not a C, because the state after phase 0 is what C describes (a sound base, real waste, some of it held) and today is plainly a grade worse.
verdict_on_bar: The floor first. React and Next are 447,102 bytes on all 560 routes, as the steward says (seven files, summed here). The frame is not 64 KB. I re-ran the cut simulation on the built chunks: a signed-in screen that is the frame alone (the account's Billing) lands at about 616,000 bytes, so the frame is about 169 KB. The 64 KB is only what leaves when one part is dropped. So 650,000 is the frame plus 34 KB of a screen's own code, not plus 140 KB. It is tighter than the steward believed and I keep it: about 200 KB gzip, of which 134 KB is the framework. Kept as well: 800,000 by idle on the home, the builder at 1,800,000 (about 1.6 MB by modules plus 12%; I could not check that floor closer than 100 KB either way), 0 prefetches at rest, 6 notice requests an hour, 100 rows a list, and Google's good line in production. Tightened in five places. (1) zod. 'At most 160 routes, on a list that may only shrink' is a B by the steward's own rule. Only 4 of 332 admin client files call a schema, and my re-run leaves zod on 118 screens outside the builder, brought by a helper that shares a file with a schema: 117 to 150 KB each. New bar: at most 60 routes, each named with the schema it runs. (2) A product's editor gets its own line, 1,100,000. Its only ceiling was 1,300,000, set where the cuts happen to land (about 1.26 MB), and about 290 KB of that is zod and the page model, which the screen's own code does not run. (3) The builder's document: 445,000, not 480,000. Step 2.30's own figure for its texts gives 439,000. (4) Requests at rest are held on eight screens, not on the home alone. The pages list (46) and settings (44) are today's worst. (5) By idle, the builder gets a number, 2,500,000. Step 2.29 moves 435 KB to after first paint and nothing counted it. Added: the words in Norwegian (45.3 KB shared today, against 34.0 in English), what a save sends back, a frame-alone figure, and a time figure in the lab until production has 100 loads a kind. Loosened: nothing. Not measurable as written: the steward's request budgets on orders, a product's editor and the builder have no step that creates them, and the production figure needs loads that do not exist before opening. AMENDED BY THE PANEL'S CRITIC, so that one thing has one number in every area: 5: words a screen is handed: handed against named, counted from source in both languages: at most 1.1 times the groups a screen's parts name on the five budgeted screens and at most 1.25 times at every site that hands over 50 KB; the browser's record stays as a cross-check that may only rise; shared words at most 15.5 KB and 16 KB. 4: sign-in English (shortfall 4): only the routes that draw a part that reads it: 2 today, each named. 6: the notice poll: 6 an hour; with a no the measure is short.

measures.name: First scripts of a plain signed-in screen
measures.today: Median of the 449 admin routes: 1,152,953 bytes raw (recomputed from .next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json). The store home 1,194,862 (360,861 gzip), orders 1,186,348, products 1,167,291, settings 1,140,078, the platform home 1,149,116. A screen that is the frame alone (the account's Billing) is 1,123,681. React and Next are 447,102 of each, on all 560 routes. 481 KB of every screen is Supabase's client, zod and the page builder's English.
measures.target_a: Median at or under 650,000 bytes. The store home, orders, products, settings and the platform home each at or under 680,000 (about 205 KB gzip). The frame alone at or under 630,000. Tolerance: 15,000 bytes of room a route in the baseline.
measures.how_measured: scripts/bundle-budget.mjs over .next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json after each build, in CI. Step 1.2 creates it; it does not exist today. Also the seven screens of e2e/signed-in/admin-scripts.spec.ts.

measures.name: Script a screen has loaded by the time it is idle
measures.today: The store home 1,428,740 bytes (m/loaded.json): 1,187,034 first and 241,706 after, most of it other screens' scripts pulled by prefetch. A product's editor 2,364,674. The builder 3,454,740. Nothing budgets it: the spec reads the HTML's script tags only.
measures.target_a: The store home at or under 800,000 bytes five seconds after load, with none of Supabase's realtime, storage or database client. The builder at or under 2,500,000. Tolerance: Supabase's auth client alone (about 117 KB) after idle, and the rich text editor (435 KB) in the builder after first paint.
measures.how_measured: The by-idle case of e2e/signed-in/admin-scripts.spec.ts, on five screens in English and Norwegian. Step 1.5 creates it and step 2.31 lowers the home's figure. No step names the builder's by-idle figure yet (shortfall 2).

measures.name: First scripts of the heavy screens
measures.today: The builder 3,303,372 bytes (1,014,731 gzip), on 26 editor routes and on 13 previews that draw no editor. A product's editor 2,130,796. 90 routes are over 1,300,000 and 40 over 3,000,000. The largest is 4,274,839 (a Work invoice).
measures.target_a: The builder at or under 1,800,000, with the rich text editor and the store's language arriving after first paint. A product's editor at or under 1,100,000. No other route over 1,300,000, so at most 26 routes over that line, each named in the baseline.
measures.how_measured: scripts/bundle-budget.mjs (step 1.2): a ceiling per kind of route and the count of routes over 1,300,000, from route-bundle-stats.json.

measures.name: Code a screen downloads for something it does not draw
measures.today: By marker in first-load chunks, recounted here: Supabase's client on 432 of 449 routes, zod 432, the builder's English 423, the rich text editor 73, a whole storefront language 40, sign-in's English 442. One chunk of 1,704,595 bytes. The AI manager's chat is 496,206 bytes on first opening. Only 4 of 332 admin client files call a zod schema.
measures.target_a: Supabase on 0 routes. The rich text editor on 0. A whole storefront language on 0. Any English catalogue but common and sign-in on 0. Sign-in's English only on the routes that draw a part that reads it: 2 today, each named. zod on at most 60 routes, each named with the schema its own code runs. No first-load chunk over 600,000 bytes. The chat at or under 130,000 on first opening.
measures.how_measured: Marker strings searched in each route's first-load chunks by scripts/bundle-budget.mjs (step 1.2). The import walk src/components/admin/admin-bundle.scan.test.ts (step 1.4), with every list empty but the named zod list. e2e/signed-in/ai-manager-panel.spec.ts for the chat (step 0.11).

measures.name: Words a screen is handed, and what a save sends back
measures.today: Every store screen is handed 34.0 KB of shared words in English (45.3 KB in Norwegian) and reads about 12 KB. A product's editor is handed 238.5 KB and reads 78.9 KB. The builder is handed 311.6 KB and reads 195.4 KB. Documents: store home 165,942 characters, product editor 426,497 bytes (108 KB gzip), builder 585,943 (136 KB gzip). Each save or poll sends 51 to 66 KB of unchanged shell words again.
measures.target_a: Handed against named, counted from source in English and in Norwegian: at most 1.1 times the groups a screen's parts name on the five budgeted screens, and at most 1.25 times at every site that hands over 50 KB. The browser's record stays as a cross-check that may only rise. Shared words at most 15.5 KB (16 KB in Norwegian). Documents: store home at or under 140,000 characters, product editor 290,000 bytes, builder 445,000 with a texts object of at most 130,000. A save answers with under 20 KB of words.
measures.how_measured: The document and words baselines of e2e/signed-in/admin-scripts.spec.ts in two languages, with the bytes a save answers with. Step 1.5 creates them; steps 2.27, 2.28 and 2.30 lower them. e2e/signed-in/admin-text-fallbacks.spec.ts shows no part fell back to English.

measures.name: Requests a screen makes when nobody touches it
measures.today: 23 to 46 router prefetches per screen at rest (home 28 for 13 links, pages list 46, settings 44), and about 25 again after each save or refresh. At least 39 saves draw the whole route twice. One notice request per load and one a minute per visible tab: 60 requests and 240 statements an hour.
measures.target_a: 0 router prefetches in the 3 seconds after load on each of eight screens (home, orders, products, pages, settings, a product's editor, the builder, the platform home), and at most 2 after pointing at a link. No second draw after a save. At most 6 notice requests an hour from an untouched tab, each at most 2 statements after the account read. If the owner says no to step 2.34 the measure is short: 60 an hour is not a tolerance.
measures.how_measured: e2e/signed-in/prefetch.spec.ts: step 0.13 creates it for the home and the products rows; the other six screens have no step yet (shortfall 3). The ratchet's count of direct next/link imports (step 2.6). router-refresh.scan.test.ts (step 0.18). A clock case in e2e/signed-in/ai-manager-panel.spec.ts (step 2.34) and assistant-notices.int.test.ts (step 0.17).

measures.name: What grows with the store: rows on a list
measures.today: The Products list sends every product: about 0.9 KB of document a product, with no limit in listAdminProducts(). An estimated 4.5 MB at 5,000 products. The customers list groups every order before it cuts to 100, and the platform's Stores list loads every store. The test stores have 10 products, so nothing shows today.
measures.target_a: At most 100 rows a page on products, customers, stores and pages. A store with 500 products gets a Products document under 300,000 characters that says '100 of 500'.
measures.how_measured: The seeded case and the integration test of step 0.19; listPages() pages at 100 in step 2.17. The server area's card holds the reads behind them.

measures.name: What holds it, and the speed owners get
measures.today: 9 of 449 admin routes have a script budget, about 4% above figures that include the waste, and none of the worst four. No document, by-idle or request figure is held. The one production figure, the admin's own speed beacon, read 3.93 s LCP at p75 (INP 136 ms, TTFB 321 ms) over 52 loads on 29 and 30 October, when a plain screen loaded about 3.0 MB of script. It has not been read since, and nothing warns when it is not good. No lab figure of time exists for the admin.
measures.target_a: 449 of 449 routes in a baseline that only falls. Document, words, by-idle and request budgets on the budgeted screens in both languages. The import walk green. In production: LCP at p75 at or under 2.5 s and INP at or under 200 ms for every kind of admin screen with 100 loads or more in 28 days, with a line in the platform's briefing when one is not. Until a kind has 100 loads, a lab run with the processor slowed four times stands in: a plain screen paints within 2.5 s, and the two editors' figures are recorded and held.
measures.how_measured: scripts/bundle-budget.mjs in CI (step 1.2). admin-bundle.scan.test.ts (step 1.4). e2e/signed-in/admin-scripts.spec.ts and prefetch.spec.ts (steps 1.5 and 0.13). Platform, Usage and limits (commerce.own_speed_samples, site 'admin') and the briefing line of step 1.15. The lab run and the reading of the production table have no step yet (shortfall 3).

bar_in_a_sentence: A plain admin screen starts with at most 650 KB of script (447 KB of it is React and Next), a product's editor with at most 1.1 MB and the page builder with at most 1.8 MB; nothing is downloaded for a part the screen does not draw, a screen is handed at most 1.1 times the words its parts name, and a screen nobody touches asks the server for nothing but a notice count every ten minutes. Every route sits under a budget that only falls, and owners' real page loads paint within 2.5 seconds.
can_the_steps_reach_a: Yes, with one answer. Step 2.34 waits for your yes that the notice badge in a tab nobody touches may be up to ten minutes late; with a no the measure stays short of its bar. The builder's 1.8 MB rests on a table of cuts that step 2.30 must draw up before it starts (if it sums to under 310,000 bytes, the builder's own split joins the step), and the 28 days of real admin loads are read in step 4.5.
tolerated: React and Next: 447,102 bytes (134 KB gzip) in every screen's first scripts. It cannot go.

The admin's frame: about 169 KB on every signed-in screen. It is the rail and its icons, the menus, shortcuts, tooltips, the colour scheme, the AI manager's launcher, and the common and sign-in words in English (about 15 KB).
15,000 bytes of room a route in the script baseline, about 2% of a plain screen.
Supabase's auth client alone, about 117 KB, after the page is idle, if the trial of step 2.31 keeps it. It refreshes the session and is off the first paint.
The rich text editor, 435 KB, arrives in the builder after first paint on every open. Editing text is the builder's main job.
The builder at 1.8 MB: about 12% over what its modules need, an estimate that could be 100 KB out either way.
zod (117 KB) on the builder's 26 routes and on at most 34 other screens whose own code runs a schema.
The notice badge asks at most 6 times an hour from a tab nobody touches, so a notice can be ten minutes late there.
A touch or a keyboard press on an admin link shows the pending bar for one round trip, because links are fetched when pointed at.

Second copies of modules across chunks: 40% of the built client files, of which a browser meets about 14% while moving around. It is the chunker's trade. Measure again after the cuts, and adopt Next's flag only if a 59-screen tour falls by 10% or more.
The admin's two stylesheets, 204 KB raw (about 36 KB gzip). The styles area holds them.

A screen may be handed up to 1.1 times the words its parts name (1.25 times at a site that hands over 50 KB), counted from source. The builder's own two areas travel whole, on a short list with the reason.
owner_choices: May the notice badge in a tab nobody touches be up to ten minutes late (60 requests an hour become 6)? It shows at once on the next click and stays at one minute while an approval waits. Without this yes the poll stays at 60 an hour, at two statements each, and the measure stays short of its bar: the panel ruled that 60 an hour from each untouched tab is not a small tolerance.
The Products, Customers and Stores lists will show 100 rows at a time. Should 'select all' and a bulk action reach every row that matches, or only the 100 on the screen?

Step 2.31 keeps the session one of two ways, by trial: the auth client alone (117 KB after idle, nothing else changes) or a small refresh route (0 KB). The second changes a written sign-in rule: tokens are refreshed in the browser today. Do you want to be asked before that rule changes?
closed_shortfalls: 1. zod stays on about 144 routes, on a list that 'may only shrink', and no step shrinks it. ADDED: new step 2.46, 'Keep schemas apart from the helpers beside them, so zod loads only where a screen runs one'.
2. Step 2.30 cannot reach its own number with the parts it names. TIGHTENED: step 2.30 carries it; the text or done-when of step 3.1 changed with it.
3. Requests at rest are held on two screens and time on none. TIGHTENED: step 0.13 carries it; the text or done-when of steps 1.14, 1.15, 2.5, 2.6 changed with it.
4. Three numbers reach their bar with no room, and one count in phase 0 does not hold. TIGHTENED: step 0.9 carries it; the text or done-when of steps 0.10, 0.11 changed with it.
